metaDescription: Five desk phone stands compared by base weight, height range and case fit, for hands-free calls, reading and recipes at a home office or kitchen desk.
introParagraphs: A phone stand on a desk turns a small screen into something you can read without craning your neck or propping the phone on a mug. The best desk stands combine a base that does not slide with an angle you can set and forget. This guide compares five: the Lamicall 360 Rotation, the Lamicall height and angle adjustable stand, the OMOTON C2, the Nulaxy aluminum folding stand and the NKNZLY.

The practical differences are specific. The Lamicall 360 has a large weighted base and a two-pivot arm with 180 degrees of travel, the standard Lamicall extends up to 3.2 inches and accepts cases up to 0.71 inches thick, and the OMOTON uses 3 mm aluminum with a charging cutout. The Nulaxy works with 4 to 8 inch devices and collapses fully, while the NKNZLY is a budget pair.
We evaluated each on product specs and buyer feedback, not claimed hands-on lab work. We weighed stability on a desktop, height and angle range, case fit and how neatly each one stores.

products.name: Lamicall 360 Rotation Phone Stand
products.description:
The Lamicall 360 is the desk stand to buy if you want one that stays put. A large weighted base with anti-slip pads anchors it, and a smooth 360-degree pivot clicks into place. The two-pivot arm provides a full 180-degree angle range.

That combination means you can switch from portrait to landscape or tilt it toward you without the base creeping. The click-stop is satisfying and the pivots hold. The tradeoff is that it needs two hands to adjust, and it is bulkier than the folding picks.

It sits in a low-cost price tier despite the weighted base. Compared with the standard Lamicall, it offers more rotation but a different design. Compared with the OMOTON, it moves more freely but has no charging cutout.
products.bestFor: A permanent desk stand for calls and reading
pros: Weighted base stays put on a desk

products.name: Lamicall Height and Angle Adjustable Phone Stand
products.description:
This Lamicall stand is built around case friendliness. It accommodates phones with thick cases up to 0.71 inches, with enlarged, thickened anti-slip and anti-scratch pads. The height extends up to 3.2 inches and the stand can tilt to vertical.

Bi-folding means it folds compactly, which suits a desk that doubles as a dining table. The tradeoff is that its height gain is modest compared with taller stands. The listing is for phones rather than large tablets.

It is in a low-cost price tier. Compared with the Lamicall 360, it folds but is less planted. Compared with the Nulaxy, it handles thicker cases.
pros: Handles cases up to 0.71 inches thick
cons: Less planted than the weighted 360 model

products.name: OMOTON C2 Aluminum Phone Stand
products.description:
The OMOTON C2 uses thick 3 mm aluminum and a bigger 4.1 by 3 by 4.4 inch body for stability. A charging cutout lets you plug in a cable while the phone sits in the stand. It rotates through 270 degrees to find a viewing angle.

The open cutout is the main reason to choose it for a desk where the phone is charging all day. The hook is long enough for devices with heavy cases. The tradeoff is that the height range is limited, so the screen stays fairly low.

It sits in a low-cost price tier. Compared with the Nulaxy, it is heavier and steadier. Compared with the Lamicall 360, it offers charging but less pivoting.
products.bestFor: A phone that charges on the desk all day
pros: Charging cutout keeps the cable plugged
cons: Less flexible than a two-pivot arm

products.name: Nulaxy Full Aluminum Dual Folding Phone Stand
products.description:
The Nulaxy is a full aluminum folding stand that works with 4 to 8 inch smartphones and e-readers. The dual folding cradle collapses and adjusts to your preferred position. An anti-slip base and steady aluminum hold the phone firmly.

The compact fold suits a desk drawer or a laptop bag. The tradeoff is that folding hinges are less planted than a weighted base, and it sits in the premium price tier. It is a polished but expensive option for what it does.

It wipes clean. Compared with the NKNZLY, it is metal and steadier. Compared with the Lamicall 360, it is far more portable.
products.bestFor: Desks that move between home and office
pros: Works with phones and e-readers up to 8 inches

products.name: NKNZLY 2-Pack Foldable Phone Stand
products.description:
The NKNZLY is a two-pack so you can keep one at the office and one at home. It adjusts for an ergonomic eye level and folds fully. Anti-slip silicone pads hold the device securely.

Two stands for the lowest price tier makes it a smart spare. The tradeoff is lighter construction, so stability is a step below the weighted picks. It also has fewer specs on the listing.

It stores easily in a drawer. Compared with the Nulaxy, it costs much less but is less solid. Compared with the OMOTON, it lacks a charging cutout.
pros: Two stands in the lowest tier

buyingCriteria.explanation: A heavier base with non-slip padding resists tipping, and plastic stands wobble versus aluminum. The Lamicall 360 has a large weighted base and the OMOTON uses 3 mm aluminum. On a desk you tap and type near, weight matters. Add weight to the base for heavy tablets.

Check the width range and thickness including the case. The standard Lamicall accepts cases up to 0.71 inches thick, while the Nulaxy works with 4 to 8 inch devices. Universal fit is marketing, so verify measurements. A rugged case may exceed a narrow cradle.

Desktop stands typically cover about 4.3 to 6.7 inches of height, and the standard Lamicall extends up to 3.2 inches. The Lamicall 360's 180-degree arm range gives flexible tilt. Pick more range if you share the desk. Fixed angles are simpler.
A charging slot or open design lets you charge during long calls. The OMOTON C2 has a charging cutout. Check that your cable plugs in cleanly. A cutout saves you from unplugging.

Foldable models carry easily but are usually lighter and less stable. The Nulaxy and NKNZLY fold, while the Lamicall 360 stays put. Decide whether the stand leaves the desk. A permanent stand favors weight.

Silicone or rubber padding avoids scratches on your phone and desk. The standard Lamicall uses thickened anti-scratch pads, and the NKNZLY uses silicone. Check the contact points. Cheap hard plastic can mark the finish.

howWeEvaluated.title: Desktop stability
howWeEvaluated.description: The Lamicall 360's weighted base and the OMOTON's 3 mm aluminum scored highest, while the NKNZLY scored lower. We judged from specs and buyer feedback, not lab trials.

howWeEvaluated.title: Angle and height range
howWeEvaluated.description: We scored adjustment range. The Lamicall 360's 180-degree arm and the OMOTON's 270-degree rotation scored well. The standard Lamicall's 3.2 inch extension scored in the middle.

howWeEvaluated.title: Case compatibility
howWeEvaluated.description: We considered stated case limits. The standard Lamicall's 0.71 inch limit scored highest, while stands with no stated limit scored lower. Case-friendly pads earned credit.

howWeEvaluated.title: Storage and portability
howWeEvaluated.description: The Nulaxy and NKNZLY fold, while the Lamicall 360 is bulkier. The strongest pick, the Lamicall 360, outranks the most basic, the NKNZLY, on stability.

howWeEvaluated.title: Value for the price tier
howWeEvaluated.description: The NKNZLY is lowest-cost, the Lamicall and OMOTON are low-cost, and the Nulaxy is premium. We credit stands that stay steady.

cards.label: Weighted or thick metal
cards.text: The Lamicall 360 and OMOTON stay put for typing near the phone. They are not pocket stands.

cards.label: Folding
cards.text: The Nulaxy, NKNZLY and standard Lamicall fold away. Recommendation: weighted for a fixed desk, folding if the desk is shared.

howToChoose.subheading: For a Home Office Desk Specifically

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: A weighted base, an angle you can set quickly and a charging path. Avoid stands that shift when you type nearby.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The Lamicall 360 offers stability and travel, and the OMOTON adds a charging cutout. Choose the Lamicall 360 for calls and the OMOTON for charging.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: The desk is your daily workspace, where the Lamicall 360's base earns its place, or you want the Nulaxy's aluminum fold.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: You want a spare, where the NKNZLY 2-Pack at the lowest tier is enough.

faq.q: How do I choose between a weighted stand and a folding one?
faq.a: Weighted stands like the Lamicall 360 stay put on a desk. Folding stands like the Nulaxy travel easily. Choose by whether the stand moves.

faq.q: How much should a desk stand cost?
faq.a: A desk stand is a low-cost accessory. The NKNZLY at the lowest tier works as a spare, while the Lamicall models are low-cost and sturdier. Pay more for stability.

faq.q: How do I clean a stand?
faq.a: Wipe with a damp cloth and dry. Clean silicone pads so they keep gripping. Avoid solvents on the pads.
The standard Lamicall accepts cases up to 0.71 inches, and the OMOTON hook holds heavy cases. Measure your case first. Universal fit is marketing.

faq.q: Can I use a stand for a tablet?
faq.a: Some stands support up to 8 inches, like the Nulaxy. Heavy tablets in cases need a weighted base. Check the stated weight limit.
Light bases slide on smooth desks. A weighted base and non-slip pads fix it. A damp cloth can also clean slippery feet.

faq.q: Should I buy a stand with a charging cutout?
faq.a: If your phone charges at the desk, yes. The OMOTON C2 leaves the port open. Otherwise it is not necessary.
